text.checkText: The task is done on every due day for two weeks, checked in the weekly review.
text.exampleNote: This is an example: a warehouse with one area manager, two shift leads and three team leaders over the last three weeks. Add your own leader and it disappears, or clear it now.

levels.name: Team leader
levels.note: Leads a team on the floor, every shift.

levels.name: Shift lead
levels.note: Leads the team leaders of one shift.

levels.name: Area manager
levels.note: Leads an area across its shifts.

levels.name: Site manager
levels.note: Leads the site or the hotel.

frequencies.name: Every shift, after the shift start
Monthly on a day of the month

reasons.name: Firefighting
reasons.meaning: The day ran the leader: an urgent problem took the time the standard needed. Firefighting that comes back is a problem nobody owns yet.
moves: Protect the huddle and the first check of the shift: they go ahead even on a bad day.
Write down what you fought today and take the fire that comes back to 5 Whys.
Agree with your manager which task may drop on a red day, and which never does.
reasons.question: Which fire did you fight twice this week, and who owns its cause?

reasons.name: Absent, not covered
reasons.meaning: The leader was away and nobody did the standard for them: the routine depends on one person.
moves: Name a deputy for every leader on the board.
Hand the printed card to the deputy with the handover.
Review the deputy’s day the same way as the leader’s.
reasons.question: Who runs this standard tomorrow if the leader is ill?

reasons.name: No time
reasons.meaning: The standard does not fit the day: more minutes are planned than the job leaves.
moves: Compare the planned minutes with the guide share of the day for this level.
Move the task to a quieter hour, or make it weekly instead of daily.
Take away work that is not the leader’s (admin, chasing) before you cut the standard.
reasons.question: What did you do in the minutes this task should have had?

reasons.name: Not relevant today
reasons.meaning: The task did not apply today. It is left out of the adherence, but a task that is often not relevant is a standard to change.
moves: Look at the tasks marked not relevant most often: do they belong to this level?
Turn a task that applies only on some days into a weekly or monthly one.
Remove what nobody misses after two weeks.
reasons.question: If this task is so often not relevant, what would be?

reasons.name: Forgot
reasons.meaning: The standard is not a habit yet: nothing in the day reminds the leader of it.
moves: Carry the printed card and tick it at the board.
Put the standard in the calendar with the calendar file.
Tie the task to a fixed event: right after the huddle, before the handover.
reasons.question: What happens just before this task every day that could remind you of it?

unrecorded.meaning: Nobody marked these tasks on their day. A standard that is not checked off cannot be reviewed, so it counts as missed.
moves: Tick the card at the end of the shift, before the handover.
Check off on the phone right after each task.
The next level asks for the card in its daily meeting.
unrecorded.question: When in the shift do you have two minutes to tick the card?

tips: A standard for the leader, too.

Leader standard work is the routine of each leader written down: what, when, how long and what done looks like. The share of the day it fills falls with the level (about 80 % for a team leader, 50 % for a shift lead, 25 % for a manager, after David Mann).
Pick your sector and level, then change the times and tasks to your day. Save it as a template file to give it to the next leader.
Done, missed with a reason, or not due. What is not marked by the end of the day counts as missed (not recorded).
Once a week the manager looks at the adherence and the task missed most, with the leader, and writes down what they agreed. The point is help, not control.
A task missed three times in two weeks goes to the Action Tracker: either the day needs help or the standard needs changing.
